title: Vendor Comms & Escrow Pathway Sync
summary: Kickoff to align on MSA/DPA redlines, escrow expectations for privileged key access, pricing approval path and onboarding timeline; agreed to send redlines and security packet and schedule a follow-up with engineering for escrow technical validation.
topics: DPA and data residency / egress fees
transcript:
Header: 2027-11-17 11:00 AM PST | Duration: 1:02 | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Morales (Redwood) — Priya Patel, Liam O'Neill, Omar Reyes, Sonia Gupta (Arcadia)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, um, quick intro — I'm Maya, account exec on this — Diego from our solutions team will cover the more technical bits.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Hi all, thanks. We scheduled this to understand the legal gating items and how escrow would work with your private offering, and to get clarity on internal pricing approvals.
[00:20] Diego Morales: Great. I'll keep the tech short but yeah, we do sometimes get asked about privileged keys or model escrow, especially for regulated customers.
[01:05] Liam O'Neill: Right, for us the big ones are: can we keep keys on our HSM? Do you support customer-managed KMS? And what exactly would be in escrow — model artifacts, runtime, or admin consoles?
[01:22] Diego Morales: Short answer: yes to customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; we integrate via standard KMS APIs and can support HSM-based key wrapping. For escrow, we typically offer a code-and-config escrow package — not model weights by default — but we can discuss including runtime artifacts depending on risk profile. There was a little noise there — sorry — the exact items are negotiable.
[02:10] Sonia Gupta: From legal, our template has a couple of nonstandard asks — 1) an MSA clause to permit on-demand audit access, 2) stronger data deletion proof for egress scenarios, and 3) escrow terms that allow us to retrieve artifacts if you cease operations.
[02:34] Maya Chen: Understood. We have a vendor playbook: we can grant audit logs and extended retention for a fee, and for escrow there's a standard third-party escrow that we can route through. The MSA language, though, around audit access and termination-triggered escrow release — we'll need to see the redlines.
[03:05] Priya Patel: Also pricing — FinOps flagged that any additional escrow or HSM support may be add-on priced, which will push it past our monthly target. Omar, can you remind them of our approval threshold?
[03:16] Omar Reyes: Yeah, threshold is $85k ARR to be auto-approved by procurement; above that it needs FinOps + Legal exec sign-off. We're trying to keep this pilot under that until we validate latency and SLOs.
[03:40] Diego Morales: For a pilot, we can provide a limited Dedicated pool with soft SLA and usage caps; we can also set cached prefixes to reduce token cost during eval. The Dedicated + HSM option is typically a reserved-capacity contract though.
[04:28] Liam O'Neill: What's the fallback if you don't meet latency targets during pilot — do you have rollback or fallback models? We need to avoid patient-impacting failures.
[04:38] Diego Morales: Yes — smart routing policy: requests can fall back to a lower-latency smaller model in the same region, and we expose tracing to help triage. For mission-critical flows we recommend a canary + automatic fallback policy.
[05:00] Sonia Gupta: Back to escrow: our counsel wants explicit indemnity if escrowed artifacts include any third-party binaries. Do you include licences in escrow?
[05:12] Maya Chen: Typically not; but we can include a manifest that lists third-party dependencies and license metadata. Full indemnity language depends on vendor counsel, so we'll need to exchange redlines.
[05:42] Priya Patel: Can you also confirm data residency? We need all PHI to stay in-region (US-East). Any cross-border backups?
[05:50] Diego Morales: Private deployment option supports VPC in customer region. Backups can be configured to stay in-region; egress fees apply for cross-region replication. I'll put details in the security packet we send.
[06:30] Maya Chen: Quick note — we have SOC 2 Type II attestation and can provide the report under NDA; FedRAMP is a longer pathway.
[06:45] Liam O'Neill: SOC 2 is fine for now. What about SSO and RBAC? We need role separation for operator accounts.
[06:54] Diego Morales: We integrate with SAML/SCIM for SSO and allow RBAC with fine-grained roles. Privileged operator access can be audited and limited.
[07:20] Sonia Gupta: On MSA redlines, there are three main asks: (a) liability cap carve-out for data breaches, (b) stronger SLA credit definitions, and (c) faster termination timelines if data residency is violated.
[07:38] Maya Chen: I hear you. For liability caps we typically have a standard carve-out; SLA credit definitions — we can clarify metrics. Termination for residency violations we'll need to discuss with product. I'll flag those.
[08:10] Priya Patel: Omar — if escrow + HSM ends up being an add-on, can we re-scope the pilot to keep costs low but still validate controls?
[08:19] Omar Reyes: Yes, we prefer to run a functional pilot against non-prod PHI-scrubbed data first, then add HSM/escrow for the production ramp.
[09:00] Maya Chen: That sounds like a reasonable path. Next steps from our side: we'll send the security packet, a proposed MSA redline, and a pricing pathway that outlines pilot vs production.
[09:12] Sonia Gupta: Want to note: timeline — Legal review windows are 10 business days; procurement adds another 5 typically. We want to aim for production by end of Q1 so the pilot needs signoff this quarter.
[09:28] Diego Morales: If you want, we can run a short technical pre-flight (30–60 min) for your infra team to validate HSM/KMS integration. That would speed the back-and-forth.
[09:44] Liam O'Neill: Yes please — schedule that with our infra lead (I'll share contact). Also we want to do a short benchmark showing 99th percentile latency for the 2k token path.
[10:05] Maya Chen: We'll put that into the technical checklist.
[10:20] Priya Patel: A couple of procurement specific Qs: are there milestone-based invoice options? We don't want a big upfront reserved commitment for pilot.
[10:31] Maya Chen: For pilots we can do a monthly consumption model or a small reserved pilot with minimal commit. Production Dedicated typically has a reserved contract, but there's flexibility.
[11:02] Omar Reyes: If pricing shows a clear per-token delta vs the hosted option, that helps our FinOps model. We'll want the unit economics in a spreadsheet.
[11:17] Maya Chen: We'll share a granular cost model with token and embedding unit rates, plus add-on line items for HSM and escrow.
[11:40] Sonia Gupta: Last legal note — we may request an amendment to the DPA for retention and disposition proof. Can you provide a data deletion certificate or logs?
[11:52] Diego Morales: We can provide audit logs and deletion confirmation; for Private deployments the logs are customer-accessible and can be shipped as part of the report.
[12:15] Priya Patel: Good. Let's capture action items and who owns each.

Action items discussed inline:
[12:30] Maya Chen: To recap — Maya to send MSA redline and security packet; Diego to schedule infra pre-flight and send technical checklist; Maya to include pricing spreadsheet; Arcadia (Sonia/Priya) to provide legal redlines and infra contact; Omar to confirm internal approval thresholds and sign-off timeline.

[12:55] Priya Patel: Ok thanks. If we get the redlines within two business days we'll circulate internally.
[13:10] Maya Chen: Great. We'll target sending materials by Friday. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the infra pre-flight.
[13:20] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional speech recognition errors and minor speaker misattribution; some product names transcribed as generic terms (e.g., "Private deployment" sometimes captured as "private deploy").
